label: prf:neutron-proton-mass-splitting
title: Proof of neutron proton mass splitting
html:
Proof. The proton possesses quark content \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}; the neutron possesses \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}. At the quark level, the crossing types evaluate as:

  • \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}: same-type \to \sigma (eigenvalue q).
  • \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}: same-type \to \sigma^{-1} (eigenvalue q^{-1}).
  • \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}: mixed \to \tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma + \sigma^{-1}).

Replacing one \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u} crossing with one \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} crossing shifts the quantum dilogarithm by \Delta\Phi = \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) - \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}).

The ground-state configurations are \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d} (proton, \Phi_{\mathfrak{p}} = -0.8785) and \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} (neutron, \Phi_{\mathfrak{n}} = -1.2261). This yields |\Delta\Phi| = 0.3476.

At the quark level, a more negative \Phi implies greater confinement energy (rather than reduced binding, as occurs at the nuclear level). The \mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} crossing (\sigma^{-1}) generates more confinement than the \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u} crossing (\sigma). This excess makes the neutron heavier.

The scale \alpha = m_e \times 8G governing nuclear binding also dictates the quark-level confinement splitting:

  \Delta m = 3.7445 \times 0.3476 \approx 1.302 \;\mathrm{MeV}.

This prediction compares to the CODATA value \Delta m = 1.2934 MeV, an error of 0.63\%. \square

Provenance and scope (2026-08-25). This proof cites no live witness and its stated agreement is not currently reproducible.

The witness named here until now, atom-mass-complete-wedderburn.witness.json, is absent from computations/. It was not, however, never produced: it was added on 2026-04-10 in commit 1359fe23ac under folio-assistant/computations/ and left the tree with the platform code in the miga migration (recovery and analysis). It is nonetheless the wrong artifact for this block: it is an atomic-mass witness of 20 atom rows, cited by a quark-level computation, and the recovered file contains no quark \Phi values at all. So this block has no usable witness either way.

Re-deriving the two \Phi values from the crossing rules stated above (computations/pn_splitting_proof_provenance_probe.py) pins the reading and then fails to confirm the result. Convention C with the suffix-inclusive \Phi_1 reproduces \Phi_{\mathfrak{p}} = -0.8785233 against the -0.8785 quoted above — exact at the quoted precision, and the only one of eight readings that lands. The same reading gives \Phi_{\mathfrak{n}} = -1.2677888, not the -1.2261 quoted. Because the reading is pinned by the proton, this is not reading ambiguity.

Consequently:

source \lvert\Delta\Phi\rvert \Delta m (MeV) vs CODATA
as stated above 0.3476 1.3016 +0.63\%
re-derived, convention C 0.3892655 1.4576 +12.7\%
re-derived, convention D 0.3354835 1.2562 -2.87\%

The derivation is also convention C throughout, which the owner ruling of 2026-08-15 excised in favour of convention D (z = q^3/(q^2 + 1)); under D the block's own construction gives -2.87\%, not +0.63\%.

Scope (a): eight readings were tried, which is not an exhaustive exclusion, and no replacement value is proposed here. What is established is that the +0.63\% figure cannot currently be checked and should not be cited as a confirmed prediction.
